sections.heading: C — Right-of-way
sections.markdown:
## C — Right-of-way

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
A diverging diamond interchange removes the troublesome left-turn movements of a standard interchange, which leaves fewer conflict points with other vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Right-of-way rules decide who goes first and who waits when drivers or pedestrians meet where no sign or signal controls traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
The law only says who must yield; it never grants anyone the right-of-way, not even a driver facing a green light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers who are already inside an intersection you are approaching. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, who have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk; come to a full stop and let them pass safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Take extra care around children, seniors and people with disabilities, and never assume a pedestrian can see or hear your vehicle or a crossing signal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
A white cane or a guide dog is the usual sign that a pedestrian is blind or deaf-blind. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
On the road a bicycle counts as a vehicle with many of the rights and duties of a motor vehicle, but a bicyclist on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk has the rights and duties of a pedestrian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
When you merge with or cross a designated bike lane to make a turn, you must yield to bicyclists in that lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
At a four-way stop the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if vehicles arrive together, the one on the left yields to the one on the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A01
No matter who has the right-of-way, every driver is still responsible for avoiding a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A01
An uncontrolled intersection has no stop signs or lights; when vehicles reach it at the same moment, the vehicle on the left lets the vehicle on the right go first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A01
Before turning left, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to smaller oncoming road users like bicyclists and motorcyclists, judging their speed and distance carefully. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A01
A left-turning driver yields to all oncoming traffic unless holding a green arrow or having arrived first at a four-way stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A01
When changing lanes or passing, yield to vehicles already in the lane you want, and do not move over if another driver would have to slow for you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A01
When merging, yield to every vehicle on the road you are joining, and do not merge if it would force someone to slow down. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A01
When backing up, yield to all vehicles near enough to be a hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A01
On a steep road too narrow for two vehicles, the downhill driver yields by backing to a wider spot or stopping to leave room, unless it is more practical for the uphill driver to return to a turnout. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A01
Yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or flashing red, blue, white or yellow lights by pulling to the right edge and stopping where possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A01
If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are inside an intersection, continue through the intersection first and then pull over. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A01
Passing an emergency vehicle stopped beside the road, try to leave at least one empty lane between you, or slow to a safe speed and use care if you cannot change lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A01
Unless emergency personnel direct otherwise or conditions prevent a lane change, slow to 25 MPH when the posted limit is 45 MPH or less, or to 20 MPH below the limit when it is above 45 MPH. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A01
Yield to service and maintenance vehicles that are working and showing flashing yellow and blue lights, and take extra care when approaching or passing them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A01
Snow plows can be hidden by the blowing snow they throw up, and passing working plows that are staggered diagonally in formation is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A01
Stop at least 20 feet away from a school bus that has stopped with red lights flashing, and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A01
The school bus stop rule applies on your side of the road, the opposite side or at an intersection ahead, unless a median or other physical barrier separates you from the bus. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A01
After a school bus turns off its lights, look carefully for children near the bus and crossing the road before you move. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A01
Yield to a transit bus that is signaling to pull into a traffic lane when the yield sign on its rear is lit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A01
In a work or construction zone, protect crews and other road users by shifting your lane position away from workers and slowing down for obstacles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

items.why: Arrival order and left-versus-right yielding are learned best through picture scenarios, not definitions.
Two speed rules keyed to the posted limit are easy to swap and need targeted number drills.
